text:
maria gonzalez: Quick idea — let's run a small matrix of smoke + saturate runs to calibrate sane defaults for RPM/TPM and burst windows. Support is seeing customers hit bursts and then billing counters blow up.
kevin li: +1. Do you mean separate open-loop (fixed RPS) and closed-loop (concurrency-driven) tests?
samir patel: yeah. we should capture 429s, 5xx, p95/p99 latency and token accounting deltas. also test with KV-cache warm vs cold.
jonathan park: also include an auth failure curve — we had a case where intermittent 401s during load triggered billing mismatch because retries counted.
maria gonzalez: Good call. Proposed matrix:
- smoke: 30s at target RPS to validate routing/fallbacks
- ramp: 5m ramp until sustained 95th percentile latency > target
- saturate: 10m at 2x expected peak to observe rate-limiting behavior
- burst window tests: apply short 5s spikes at 5x and measure token/credit consumption
kevin li: For reproducibility add: header X-Client-ID + randomized API key set so we can test per-key quotas. Also record the request-id header and the backend model variant.
samir patel: here's a tiny k6 smoke snippet we can start with:
```js
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export default function() {
  let res = http.post('https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate', JSON.stringify({prompt: 'hello'}), {headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer ${KEY}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-Client-ID': 'load-test-01' }});
  console.log(`${res.status} ${res.headers['x-request-id'] || ''}`);
  sleep(1);
}
```
jonathan park: Nice. Add a counter to emit how many tokens were billed (we can pull from response or from billing logs after the run).
kevin li: For metrics: expose -> client_rpm, client_tpm (tokens per minute), 429_rate, 503_rate, p95lat, p99lat, billing_delta, cache_hit_rate. We'll correlate billing_delta with request-ids.
support-bot: FYI: opened SUPPORT-1289 to surface customer repros. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUPPORT-1289
ratebot: reminder — dedicated customers have different burst windows; include a test vector for dedicated vs hosted (same RPS but different quota).
maria gonzalez: Repro steps for the team:
1) provision test keys in the load namespace (tag keys with test-run id)
2) run smoke -> ramp -> saturate scripts, capture traces and request-ids
3) run billing extractor: `python tools/extract_billing.py --start <ts> --end <ts> --keys test-*`
4) compare token counts with service-side counters `curl https://ops-api/usage?client=load-test-01`
5) annotate runs in the runbook with whether 429s occurred and if fallback routing triggered
jonathan park: We should also test retry behavior client-side: add a variant with exponential backoff retries to see how it affects TPS and billing.
samir patel: One oddball we've seen: short bursts that exceed token-window cause the gateway to return 429 but the downstream started processing some requests — those still got billed. Need to verify idempotency of billing on early abort.
kevin li: Ops note: when running saturate, use the staging model variants only (don't point at prod) and throttle calls to admin endpoints. Also add a kill-switch in the script to stop immediately on spike 5xx > 30% for 1m.
maria gonzalez: I'll schedule a 1h run tomorrow 10am PT. Volunteers? need someone to watch billing logs and someone to triage 429 traces.
kevin li: I can watch billing logs.
samir patel: I'll watch traces and toggle KV cache warm/cold.
jonathan park: I'll prepare the retry/backoff variant.
maria gonzalez: Great. After run we'll propose default conservative RPM/TPM + burst window based on where 429 becomes non-trivial and where p95 jumps > 2x. Will post results in #eng-sre and ping @product for thresholds. :thumbsup:
